paragraphs: Existence has two faces: it demands material resources, shelter, and protection, yet offers comfort, pleasure, and enjoyment when these needs are satisfied. Both are real parts of embodied life, but neither its demands nor its rewards constitute its ultimate purpose. Humanity’s mission is to honor the creator’s likeness within us and extend the creator’s presence outward. Accepting the challenges of survival and meeting our needs sustain our existence and thus enable this mission.

Overemphasizing life’s demands can intensify anxiety, becoming absorbed in its rewards can foster materialism and addiction, and ignoring its purpose leaves life a withering shell, empty of meaning. A healthy approach is to face the challenges of survival with courage, use our gifts and intelligence wisely to work and serve, and appreciate the satisfactions life offers. Above all, we must keep our mission in view and find meaning only in the creator.

Sources across traditions offer different perspectives on the relationship between needs, enjoyment, and purpose. The Bible acknowledges our need for food and clothing but teaches us to seek God’s kingdom first and glorify God through good works [41]. Ecclesiastes presents enjoyment in food, drink, and work as God’s gift while directing us to revere God and keep his commandments [42]. Aristotle distinguishes wealth and pleasure from life’s highest good: resources support a good life, but living well means using our abilities wisely and virtuously in pursuit of human flourishing [32]. Augustine locates our ultimate meaning in God and warns that repeated indulgence can turn pleasure into a pursuit beyond bodily need [27]. From the East, the Great Learning places virtue above the wealth that provides for material needs, making self-cultivation the foundation of a well-ordered life. This cultivation extends outward through the family and state toward peace throughout the world [47].

A healthy life therefore neither regards the struggle to survive as a pointless burden nor makes life’s pleasures its highest goal. It meets existence’s demands and enjoys its rewards under the guidance of its mission: to honor the creator’s likeness within us and extend the creator’s presence outward.
